cues: A slender frame supports paired rotating wheels, while aligned components keep the moving structure stable under changing loads.
Interlocking gears convert rotation into useful torque, a compact transmission principle found across many kinds of vehicles.
Smooth contours reduce resistance during travel, making careful shaping valuable for efficient movement through air or water.
A balanced steering assembly redirects a moving vehicle through linked controls without disturbing its central structure.
Rotating shafts and carefully aligned bearings reduce vibration as mechanical power drives the vehicle forward.
A lightweight metal framework supports wheels and gearing, combining rigidity with efficient movement over uneven routes.
Efficient propulsion depends on transferring power smoothly from a turning input to a rotating drive element.
Streamlined components and balanced mass help reduce drag and keep motion steady at changing speeds.
